questions.q: Why does Mara inventory Hartwell's identity footprint before attempting any consolidation?
options: Because inventorying is required by law before any IT project
Because consolidating without first counting what exists would carry forward every orphaned account and inconsistency, just hidden behind a federation layer afterward
Because Azure AD and AWS IAM cannot be queried at the same time
Because the board explicitly forbade any consolidation work this quarter
questions.explain: Skipping the inventory step means every existing problem gets carried forward into the consolidated view, just harder to find because it's now behind a federation layer instead of visible in two separate consoles.

questions.q: What does Hartwell's Entra ID (Azure AD) footprint reveal?
options: A small, perfectly maintained tenant with no issues at all
About 1,400 user accounts, roughly 85 overlapping security groups, and dozens of service principals/managed identities, several over-scoped for their actual task
Zero service principals, since Hartwell doesn't use any automation
A tenant that was created last week with no history
questions.explain: The tenant shows years of unmanaged growth: ~1,400 accounts including stale disabled ones, ~85 overlapping/poorly named groups, and dozens of service principals, some with far broader Azure RBAC roles than their task requires.

questions.q: What specific AWS risk pattern does Mara's boto3 query surface across Hartwell's three AWS accounts?
options: Buckets with public read access
IAM users still authenticating with active, long-lived access keys that have never been rotated
Unused EC2 instances running up cost
Missing CloudTrail logging
questions.explain: The pagination query across list_users and list_access_keys flags IAM users with an active access key older than 180 days — exactly the long-lived-credential risk pattern that federated roles exist to replace.

questions.q: What is the single biggest finding from this identity mapping exercise, bigger than any one bad account or stale key?
options: Hartwell uses too many cloud providers
Hartwell has no single system of record for identity — answering 'what can this person access?' requires checking Entra ID and three separate AWS accounts with nothing keeping them in sync
Hartwell's employees have weak passwords
Hartwell's AWS accounts are not part of an AWS Organization
questions.explain: The real finding is structural: there's no authoritative, synchronized source for identity across Entra ID and the three AWS accounts, which is exactly why the board's mandate called for a consolidated view, not a one-time cleanup.

questions.q: How many separate AWS accounts make up Hartwell's AWS Organization, and what is each one for?
options: One account covering everything
Three accounts: Hartwell-Corp for general workloads, Hartwell-OT-Analytics where SCADA telemetry lands, and Hartwell-DevTest for lower environments
Five accounts, one per Hartwell department
Two accounts, split only by geographic region
questions.explain: Hartwell-Corp, Hartwell-OT-Analytics, and Hartwell-DevTest each grew their own IAM users, groups, and roles independently with no shared naming convention between them.
